claims.claim: A consistently negative N1002K protein score provides strong variant-specific evidence.
claims.support: All four current models score the substitution negatively and reproduce the original control scores. ESMC 600M/6B rank it relatively low among matched N-to-K substitutions.
claims.challenge: 71.6–89.8% of background substitutions score negatively. Candidate rank changes by model and comparison set; 6B places K second-most compatible among alternatives at this constrained position.
claims.falsifier: Candidate effect is not distinguishable from appropriate measured retained-function controls, or endogenous assays retain function.
claims.stop: Do not promote pathogenicity or folding rescue from sign, raw magnitude, rank or model voting.
claims.reopen: Independent endogenous abundance/localization/segregation evidence with measured controls.
claims.next_action: Test candidate and retained/impaired controls in the same relevant assay; preserve matched-background and secondary-control sensitivity.

claims.claim: Passing the small primary model challenge generalizes to broader function discrimination.
claims.challenge: Adding the secondary controls still breaks separation in 8/12 comparisons; model/window outputs are dependent and no clinically labeled background exists.
claims.falsifier: New blinded relevant control panel fails prespecified discrimination or calibration.
claims.stop: No sensitivity/specificity, clinical probability or therapeutic-effect estimate from these scores.
claims.reopen: Independent assay-labeled benchmark and a frozen decision rule with a held-out evaluation.
claims.next_action: Retain expanded controls and record all model/window results; do not select only models that support the candidate.

claims.claim: HT29 BUB1B cross-modal retrieval is explained entirely by broad shared response.
claims.support: Correlation attenuates from .3712 to .1510 after mean plus ten-component removal; TTK is a strong original neighbor.
claims.challenge: BUB1B remains rank 2–5 in both directions across all five PRIME views, including removal of 13 selected cell-cycle/stress features.
claims.falsifier: Independent perturbation/restoration retains target-specific segregation effects after matching growth, viability and editing controls.
claims.stop: Do not discard favorable HT29 counterevidence, but do not qualify a non-cancer MVA model from one guide and one passing batch.
claims.reopen: Independent guide or non-cutting perturbation, restoration and relevant non-cancer functional endpoints.
claims.next_action: Use HT29 for attribution/assay development, followed by relevant model qualification.

claims.claim: MCF7 everolimus reversal is a robust BUB1B-rescue rationale.
claims.support: Original rank 7 and feature-removal rank 8; MTOR mimicry stays rank 1 under all five views.
claims.challenge: BUB1B reversal falls to rank 1184 under mean plus ten-component removal; all MCF7 BUB1B queries fail QC. A375 small correlation changes sign.
claims.falsifier: Relevant qualified joint drug-plus-deficit experiments show a reproducible benefit at a justified exposure without injury; specificity survives independent perturbation/restoration.
claims.stop: Remove robust-rescue interpretation of rank 7; no cross-cell stitching, dose extrapolation or clinical promotion.
claims.reopen: Qualified same-model joint treatment, direct first-division/daughter outcomes and exposure/safety margins.
claims.next_action: Retain everolimus only as optional qualified mechanistic probe and MTOR as a pathway control.

claims.claim: More GPU work or optimized runtime establishes stronger biological evidence.
claims.support: All eight H100s executed new neural inference; complete outputs and numerical continuity checks are available.
claims.challenge: Scores share models, windows and experimental sources; compute count is not evidence independence. Anthropic toolkit was reviewed but not executed.
claims.falsifier: A new calculation fails numerical/source checks or does not answer a discriminating biological question.
claims.stop: No saturation, toolkit speedup, new experiments or independent-review claims unsupported by records.
claims.reopen: A new bounded question with fixed inputs, relevant controls and a decision it could change.
claims.next_action: Use the completed evidence to design stronger qualification tests; retain full output/telemetry and avoid reruns solely to raise compute counts.
